references.text: The term 'indignant' (Greek: ἐμβριμώμενος) describes Jesus' strong inner emotion and distress before he comes to the tomb, which also occurs in [ref:Joh 11:33|John 11:33] when he sees Mary weeping.
The description of the tomb as a 'cave' (Greek: σπήλαιον) and the stone lying over it is taken up again in [ref:Joh 11:39|John 11:39] when Jesus commands that the stone be removed.
The scene at the tomb with the stone lying across the entrance is the same as in [ref:Joh 11:44|John 11:44], where the dead come out, but the stone is still in place before the resurrection.
The same type of tomb (a cave with a stone in front) is mentioned again in [ref:Joh 20:1|John 20:1] at Jesus' own resurrection, where the stone has been taken away.
